newsitem.title: USA: AT&T raises prices on some business services.
newsitem.headline: AT&T raises prices on some business services.

text.p: AT&T Corp said Wednesday it would boost prices effective May 1 on a range of business long-distance services to offset payments to payphone owners required under a plan established by U.S. regulators.

The company said that in order to recover the higher payphone costs it would increase prices for interstate toll-free services by seven percent and prices for business international and interstate outbound services by two percent.
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) plan requires long-distance carriers to compensate payphone owners for coinless calls -- typically calling card and toll-free calls.

On April 15, local telephone companies were to begin billing AT&T and other long-distance companies for the 1.8 million payphones operated by the local companies. AT&T's share of the new costs is $26.21 per phone per month, it said.

In passing the costs along to customers, AT&T said it continued to believe the payphone increases were unjustifiably high. It pledged to roll back the price increases if it succeeds in efforts to cut the payments to payphone owners.

"While payphone owners should be fairly compensated for the cost of providing coinless calls, we believe the compensation levels set by the FCC are unreasonably high -- which is why we're challenging them in court," said Ken Sichau, AT&T vice president for business network services.
AT&T, other long-distance carriers and state regulators have appealed the FCC order. The case is scheduled to be heard in mid-May by the Court of Appeals in Washington, it said.
